newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-MILLION DOLLAR OFFER FAILS TO LIFT BOCA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILLION DOLLAR OFFER FAILS TO LIFT BOCA.

text.p: An offer of one million dollars in prize money failed to inspire the players of troubled Boca Juniors on Sunday as they crashed to yet another defeat.
Club president Mauricio Macri this week promised the squad one million dollars to divide between them if they won their remaining seven games in the Argentine championship.
But the players responded with one of their worst results yet, a 3-1 defeat against Banfield who began the weekend second-from-bottom of the table.

Boca, Argentina's best-supported club, spent an estimated $15 million in assembling their side for the competition but have slumped to 10th in the table with a mediocre record of five wins, five defeats and three draws.
They trail modest provincial outfits such as Newell's Old Boys and Rosario Central.
Coach Carlos Bilardo, who has chopped and changed his team throughout the season, left the game with the expression of a condemned man and refused to give interviews.

Boca's arch rivals River Plate, in superb form, beat San Lorenzo 4-0 to stay top, two points ahead of Lanus, an unfashionble club from the suburbs of Buenos Aires who are also playing excellent soccer.
Julio Cruz, the championship's leading scorer, grabbed two of the River goals to take his tally to 10 in the championship. Lanus, the competition's only unbeaten team, beat Ferro Carril Oeste 2-1.
